title: Token-slab fracture healer: fractional reservation + adaptive compaction for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Continuous batching and long-running chat workloads expose a persistent cause of GPU memory fragmentation in the KV cache. Small, variable-length token prefixes combined with frequent cache insertions/evictions create many sub-page holes that reduce usable KV capacity over time and increase OOM/eviction rate. Goal: introduce a low-risk, deployable KV allocation strategy and background compaction model that reduces fragmentation without violating tail latency SLOs for generation and chat.
background_and_constraints:
- Must operate on GPUs with limited spare memory and with active inference serving (no global stop-the-world).
- Compaction / migration must bound additional GPU/PCIe bandwidth and CPU impact.
- Preserve cache semantics for pinned tokens (e.g., conversation context pinned by policy).
- Integrate with continuous batching: compaction cadence should align with batch boundaries where possible to avoid adding per-request jitter.
proposed_design:
1) Fractional slab reservations: introduce 'fractional slots' within existing slab pages — each slab tracks a small number of fractional occupancy buckets keyed by token-length class and recent access heat. When a new kv entry is allocated, small entries (<= 64 bytes token payload) can be placed into fractional buckets to avoid creating many single-slot holes.

2) Soft anchoring + relocation hints: hot entries are soft-anchored to prevent immediate relocation; cold candidates get a relocation hint score computed from last-access, predicted reuse (LRU-derivative), and batch-affinity. Relocation hints are used by background compactor to prioritize moves that yield high contiguous free space.

3) Background micro-compaction lanes: run multiple prioritized compaction lanes on a node: a low-latency lane that performs very small, incremental relocations (< 2 ms bounding per invocation) synced to batch quiet windows; and a throughput lane that runs when node GPU utilization is below a threshold. Each lane enforces strict time and memory quotas.

4) Compact-and-switch shadow copy: to avoid long pauses, compaction operates by copying live entries into shadow slabs, updating indirection pointers atomically, and retiring source slabs once empty. This minimizes write amplification since only relocated entries are moved.

5) Fragmentation heuristics and triggers: compute a per-pool fragmentation_score = occupancy_variance * stale_ratio (moving average). Trigger micro-compaction when score exceeds configurable thresholds; escalate to throughput lane when score persists for N sampling periods.

6) Batching-aware scheduling: tie micro-compaction scheduling to batching telemetry. Prefer compaction during low tail-of-batch activity and avoid compaction bursts during predicted traffic spikes.

7) Telemetry & safety: expose metrics (fragmentation_score, relocations/sec, avg_relocation_latency, compaction_io_bytes, bg_compaction_cpu_pct) and add alerting playbooks for increased tail latency correlated with compaction runs.
engineering_approach:
- Implement fractional slot metadata in existing slab header (small footprint).
- Add eviction/placement path changes to favor fractional buckets for small inserts.
- Implement background compactor service with two lanes and rate limiters.
- Add indirection table safe-swap path with epoch fencing to ensure readers see either old or new pointer.
- Add compact scheduling hook into router (so compaction prefers node quiet windows).
- Add mutation telemetry and heatmap export to console and to offline analysis jobs for model-driven threshold tuning.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: compaction increases tail latency if not carefully bounded. Mitigation: strict max-ms-per-invocation, canary rollout to low-latency customers, automatic rollback if tail SLOs breach.
- Risk: shadow copy doubles short-term GPU memory. Mitigation: cap concurrent shadow allocations and fall back to in-place small relocations if headroom insufficient.
- Risk: complexity in allocator adds bugs. Mitigation: extensive unit testing of indirection swap, integration tests with long-running chat workloads, and staged rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%).
experiments_and_validation:
- Canary: enable fractional reservation mode on a small fleet (canary tag) for 2 weeks, collect fragmentation_score and evictions.
- AB test: compare token-cost/GB effective KV utilization and tail P95/P99 latencies against baseline across similar traffic shapes (chat vs short prompt).
- Stress test: synthetic workload with high churn of short tokens to measure fragmentation growth curve and compaction effectiveness.
- Validation metrics: % usable KV capacity recovered, change in evictions/sec, delta in average tokens-served-per-GB, and any change in P99 latency during compaction windows.
implementation_plan:
- Week 1-2: prototype fractional slot metadata and placement change in allocator (unit tests).
- Week 3: implement background compactor lanes and basic relocation pipeline.
- Week 4: add indirection atomic switch and safety fences; internal integration tests.
- Week 5: deploy canary with telemetry; collect metrics and iterate thresholds.
- Week 6-8: expand AB test, tune heuristics, finalize runbook and roll out to runtime-2.3 release.
acceptance_criteria: reduces fragmentation_score by >= 35% on synthetic churn workloads within 7 days
no regressions in P99 generation latency beyond 5% during steady-state traffic
evictions/sec reduced by >= 25% for chat-heavy tenants in canary cluster
telemetry surfaced in console with heatmap and alerts configured
